rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms for residential rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: City of Berkeley landlords may not use a coordinated pricing algorithm when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley. It is also unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide such an algorithm to Berkeley landlords for setting or recommending rents or occupancy levels.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to City of Berkeley landlords and residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
coverage.summary: The ordinance covers coordinated pricing algorithms used for residential dwelling units in Berkeley by Berkeley landlords, without stated unit-count, building-age, or owner-occupancy limits.

rules.exemptions: The definition excludes aggregated and anonymous reports that do not recommend future lease terms; products used to establish rent or income limits under affordable-housing guidelines; and information used for project-financing market research, appraisals, or software-development research, testing, or training, as specified.
rules.penalty: The City Attorney may seek damages, injunctive relief, restitution/return of illegal profits, civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney’s fees and costs. An aggrieved tenant may sue for subsection B violations for injunctive relief, money damages, civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney’s fees and costs.
rules.interaction: The ordinance states it does not regulate the amount of rent a landlord may charge and is not intended to prevent software that helps landlords manage units generally or uses public data.
rules.quoted_span:
Instead of waiting for court processes which may take years to resolve, this 
ordinance prohibits the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms for the purpose of 
setting rents on residential dwelling units in the city of Berkeley, to bring immediate relief 
to Berkeley tenants, as well as to put landlords on equal footing with their competitors.
rules.conflict_note: The document states the ordinance was “passed to print and ordered published” and refers to posting copies “prior to adoption,” but does not state final adoption or an effective date.
